title: Impact-Partitioned Local-Operator PINNs for Dynamic VO₂ Switching
hook: The candidate predicts that, at equal compute and comparable aggregate physics loss, preserving a high-impact residual–feature minority while compressing the redundant majority will reduce formal-OOD switching-time, front-topology, and programming-energy errors. This regime split is a hypothesis, not a reported result.
hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal, is admitted because the named downstream errors are predicted to improve even though most residual–feature packets receive less capacity than under the strongest uniform baseline. Shape (c) was viable under the matched-compute design but rejected because no result yet establishes a strict resource reduction; the fixed-budget error direction is the honest falsifiable claim.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes whether a 2D-or-higher PCM PINN can keep the electric, Joule-heating, thermal, and phase-kinetic residuals simultaneously accurate when a pulse creates moving fronts and new high-frequency modes after the initial condition — stakes: device researchers can accept the wrong switching time, programming energy, or phase topology despite a small aggregate loss, wasting compute and misdirecting device design.
gap_closure.how_closed: Corpus support is thin for oxide-PCM PINNs because C04's exemplars are compression-centric and domain-distant; C04 treats the overcomplete residual–feature bank as a downstream-error-scored high-impact minority versus a projection-redundant majority, while architectural_operator_substitution consumes the named Impact–Redundancy Packet Map to assign full-fidelity local heads to the minority and a shared low-rank bulk operator to the majority, with strongest-uniform and cheap-adaptive comparisons.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes that event order, front topology, and energy balance remain correct for held-out entire device geometries, material combinations, and pulse protocols that shift the spectrum and stiffness beyond training — stakes: reported gains may not transfer across devices or operating regimes, making the scientific conclusion non-general and the model unsafe as a design surrogate.
gap_closure.how_closed: C02 treats training–test spectral-and-stiffness overlap as the confound, constructs FEniCSx-matched whole-entity pairs plus joint geometry/material/protocol OOD groups, and uses the independent synthetic solver oracle to score event order, front topology, and programming energy; every conclusion remains bounded to the declared VO₂ PDE model rather than experimental validation.

core_mechanism: Each complete synthetic entity e=(Ω,dΩ,μ,p) is a two-dimensional-or-higher oxide-PCM device defined by its geometry Ω and signed-distance encoding dΩ, VO₂ constitutive parameters μ, and voltage pulse p(t); Gmsh and FEniCSx generate bounded mesh-converged reference trajectories, while a PyTorch parametric coordinate PINN outputs electric potential V, temperature T, phase field φ, and auxiliary Joule source q. The nonzero physics loss contains current-continuity residual R_V=∇·[σ(T,φ,|−∇V|;μ)∇V], Joule constitutive residual R_q=q−σ(T,φ,|−∇V|;μ)|∇V|², thermal residual R_T=ρc_p(T,φ;μ)∂tT−∇·[k(T,φ;μ)∇T]−q, and phase-kinetic residual R_φ=∂tφ+M(μ)δF(V,T,φ;μ)/δφ, together with declared boundary and initial residuals, so the PINN remains the core solver rather than a post-processor. Each residual is divided by s_r, whose default is the training-only interquartile scale of that equation's physical terms with machine epsilon as the zero-scale fallback; s_r is frozen before validation or formal OOD. An overcomplete uniform pilot exposes residual–feature packets b=(r,a), where r is one of the four residual channels and a is a compact space-time atom induced by the converged mesh hierarchy and pulse breakpoints; a scalar gate g_b multiplies that packet's local correction response. On training-validation entities, J_val is the mean of normalized switching-time error, GUDHI persistence-diagram front-topology distance, and normalized programming-energy error, where switching is the first terminally connected metallic path at φ_c and φ_c defaults to the equal-free-energy phase separator supplied by the declared VO₂ constitutive model rather than being tuned on test data. For packet b, δ_b is the norm of the response left after projection onto the shared bulk trunk and I_b=|∂J_val/∂g_b|δ_b is its downstream impact–redundancy score; the maximum-curvature knee of the descending cumulative I_b curve is the default deterministic split into high-impact minority H and redundant majority R, and absence of a minority-forming knee falsifies the premise rather than triggering a forced split. Under the explicitly local assumption that J_val has gate-Hessian norm bounded by the training-only measured L_g along the replacement path, the downstream fidelity loss is conditionally bounded by B_R=Σ_{b∈R}I_b+(L_g/2)||δ_R||²; B_R and its interaction remainder are reported against the full pilot, making the error decomposition rather than the partition label the contribution. C04 produces the named intermediate object O, the Impact–Redundancy Packet Map O={H,R,I_b,δ_b,m_b}, and the companion consumes O through f_hybrid=f_bulk+Σ_{b∈H}m_bΔf_b: the shared low-rank bulk trunk handles R, compactly supported full-fidelity correction heads handle H, and all four PDE/constitutive residuals are recomputed on the summed fields so cross-field coupling is never stitched after the fact. The bulk rank r_bulk defaults to the maximum-curvature knee of the training-only singular-value curve and is frozen before OOD; freed capacity is assigned to H while total parameters, collocation evaluations, optimizer updates, and GPU time are matched to a strongest uniform allocation baseline. Shared evaluation then compares the candidate with standard MLP-PINN, fixed/adaptive Fourier PINNs, causal PINN, a NeuSA-style global spectral causal PINN, the matched-capacity uniform packet model, and the cheap alternative of a globally nondimensionalized Fourier-feature PINN with residual-proportional resampling; full geometries, material combinations, pulse protocols, and complete trajectories remain indivisible groups, and FEniCSx outputs are synthetic numerical references only. Execution binding: before any δ_b or I_b is computed, form the pilot feature matrix on training entities, scale the candidate index and curve ordinate to [0,1], define each maximum-curvature knee as the interior index maximizing the absolute three-point second difference with the smallest index chosen on ties, freeze r_bulk and its corresponding shared-bulk projection subspace, define m_b as the compact-support mask of atom a on the mesh-time grid, and freeze the nonzero training-only interquartile normalizers for the three J_val components with machine epsilon as the zero-scale fallback; Step 7 reuses these bindings rather than choosing them after O.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES ledger:
P1: A small set of residual–feature packets has a heavy-tailed effect on switching time, front topology, and programming energy in pulsed VO₂ dynamics; localized fronts and nonlinear Joule/phase coupling make this plausible, but it is untested — falsification target.
P2: The declared FEniCSx electro-thermal-phase model and mesh/time convergence provide a consistent synthetic oracle for that model; they do not establish experimental truth, so claims are solver-model-bounded.
P3: The local gate-Hessian envelope L_g covers the full-to-bulk replacement path sufficiently for B_R to be informative; this is untested — falsification target, and the measured interaction remainder must be reported rather than assumed away.
OBSERVATION-MODEL premise: packet scores consume FEniCSx states and PINN residuals sampled only from pre-split training and validation entities on converged meshes and time grids; this sampling is complete only relative to the declared synthetic campaign, not unbiased over real VO₂ devices, and no formal-OOD entity contributes to s_r, φ_c, I_b, H, r_bulk, or model selection.
ESTIMAND: the target is the population mean vector of normalized switching-time error, persistence-based front-topology distance, event-order violation, and programming-energy error over the predeclared held-out whole geometry/material/protocol entities under the same FEniCSx constitutive model.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT:
The runnable naive version is a single global MLP or Fourier trunk trained on the uniformly normalized sum of R_V, R_q, R_T, and R_φ with residual-proportional collocation resampling. Branch (i): it silently assumes packets are exchangeable after nondimensionalization, which is false if an endogenous front creates a sparse set of uniquely downstream-sensitive residual–feature responses; the proposed I_b decomposition confronts that premise by preserving unique high-impact responses and compressing only projection-redundant ones. Influence-aware compression is a standard tool in other fields, but here the domain-specific unresolved structure is the differentiable map from four causally coupled PDE/constitutive residual channels to moving-front event, topology, and energy errors under whole-device OOD; if that coupling yields no distinct bound or minority, the result must be declared application-grade or negative. The design explicitly avoids reducing to XPINN spatial subdomains, VPINN weak residuals, self-adaptive loss weights, implicit-Runge–Kutta stages, global Fourier features, or causal time weighting: it retains one coupled field and changes capacity only through O.
BLOCK 3 — design rationale:
The anchor and OOD sibling share one measurement framework because the same downstream error vector defines I_b and grades formal OOD, while C02 remains a separate controlled instrument rather than a second training module. Pure residual reweighting was rejected as the occupied self-adaptive node, global NeuSA/Fourier representations do not localize t>0 generated fronts, and independent XPINN subnetworks would introduce moving-interface stitching; the bulk-plus-sparse-correction operator is the smallest mechanism that consumes O without those regressions.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Use Gmsh and FEniCSx to generate a bounded, mesh/time-converged synthetic campaign of two-dimensional VO₂ devices governed by the declared current-continuity, Joule, heat, and phase-kinetic equations; label every output as numerical reference, not experiment.
2. Split complete geometry/material/pulse/trajectory entities into training, validation, controlled-pair test, and joint formal-OOD groups before computing any scale or score.
3. Implement in PyTorch the conditioned PINN fθ(e,x,t)→(V,T,φ,q), the four explicit residuals, boundary/initial residuals, and training-only equation scales s_r; emit physical fields and device current so switching time, topology, event order, and energy propagate from the same forward solution, and freeze the three J_val normalizers from training-only interquartile scales with machine epsilon as the zero-scale fallback.
4. Train the matched-budget overcomplete uniform pilot on training entities, then evaluate its fields and downstream errors against validation-only FEniCSx references.
5. From the pilot training feature matrix, select and freeze r_bulk and the shared-bulk projection subspace using the [0,1]-scaled maximum-absolute-three-point-second-difference knee with the smallest interior index on ties; define each m_b as atom a's compact-support mask, instantiate packet gates g_b, compute δ_b and |∂J_val/∂g_b|, form I_b, and select H and R by the same deterministic cumulative-score knee rule to write O.
6. Compute B_R and the measured interaction remainder on validation entities; stop the route if no minority-forming knee exists or the decomposition does not distinguish the proposed split from uniform allocation.
7. Replace the pilot with the O-consuming architecture f_bulk+Σ_{b∈H}m_bΔf_b using the already frozen r_bulk and projection binding, and match total parameters, residual evaluations, updates, and GPU time to the uniform baseline.
8. Train the candidate with all four PDE/constitutive residuals active and run the key ablations: uniform packet allocation, partition with no local correction heads, and I_b-permuted routing, alongside MLP, Fourier/adaptive-spectral, causal, NeuSA-style, and cheap residual-resampling baselines.
9. Build C02 matched pairs that independently vary geometry, material stiffness, or pulse spectrum while holding the remaining declared factors fixed, then evaluate a separate joint whole-entity OOD group with the independent FEniCSx oracle.
10. Report switching-time error, GUDHI front-topology distance, event-order violations, programming-energy error, wall time, and peak memory; scope every result to the synthetic VO₂ model and retain a valid negative result if the uniform or cheap alternative matches the candidate.
falsification_prediction: On the bounded FEniCSx synthetic two-dimensional VO₂ campaign, train the candidate and all matched baselines with complete geometry/material/pulse entities held out for formal OOD, then measure normalized switching-time error, GUDHI front-topology distance, event-order violations, and programming-energy error. If the mechanism works, the candidate's three headline downstream errors decrease relative to the matched-capacity uniform packet baseline and the cheap residual-resampling alternative, while the partition-without-local-head ablation yields a smaller improvement. The single load-bearing variable is I_b, the packetwise downstream impact–redundancy score; the negative control randomly permutes I_b across packets before the frozen H/R split while preserving the number of local heads, parameter count, collocation budget, optimizer, seeds, and GPU time. The prediction is that this permutation returns switching-time, front-topology, and programming-energy errors toward the strongest uniform baseline; failure to do so falsifies the claimed routing mechanism without relying on an invented numeric threshold.
compute_budget: Future MVE estimate: 9 GPU-days on one 80GB-class GPU for the uniform pilot, candidate, matched baselines, key ablations, and repeated seeds, plus bounded CPU-side Gmsh/FEniCSx reference generation; paid API cost: $0. This fits the user ceiling of at most 10 GPU-days, and execution remains explicitly unauthorized.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: NeuSA projects a smooth initial-value PDE onto one truncated global Fourier basis and advances all coefficients through a NODE, whereas this candidate constructs a training-only downstream-impact packet map and uses it to place sparse local correction operators on endogenous VO₂ fronts while testing whole-entity geometry/material/protocol OOD.

The adaptive-spectral study isolates how two initial-condition gates rescale gradients in a single stiff ODE, whereas this candidate decomposes coupled electric, Joule, thermal, and phase residual–feature responses by their measured contribution to switching-time, topology, and energy error in spatial device dynamics.

The energy-embedded phase-field PINN removes temporal evolution and solves a static equilibrium with an added free-energy term, whereas this candidate retains current continuity, Joule heating, heat propagation, and phase kinetics throughout the switching trajectory and grades causal events and moving fronts.

The VO₂ work measures operando electro-thermo-mechanical domain dynamics and supports a phase-field interpretation in one suspended geometry, whereas this candidate builds a physics-residual PINN and a synthetic whole-entity OOD diagnostic without presenting solver output as experimental validation.

what_step_was_missed: NeuSA would have needed to replace its single global spectral coefficient flow with a downstream-error-derived high-impact packet map, sparse front-local correction operators, and a coupled residual fidelity decomposition validated on held-out complete VO₂ devices and pulse protocols.
alias_terms: discrete time implicit Runge Kutta PINN
